'''Leopoldo Nachbin''' (7 January 1922 – 3 April 1993) was a [[Brazilians|Brazilian]] [[mathematician]] of [[Brazilian Jews|Jewish origins]]<ref>{{cite book |year= 2018 |editor1-last= Garrido |editor1-first= Ángel |editor2-last= Wybraniec-Skardowska|editor2-first= Urszula |editor2-link=Urszula Wybraniec-Skardowska  |title= The Lvov-Warsaw School: Past and Present |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=ueZfDwAAQBAJ |publisher= Birkhäuser |page=782|isbn= 978-3-319-65429-4}}</ref>  who dealt with [[topology]] and [[harmonic analysis]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.im.ufrj.br/doc/nachbin.htm |title=Archived copy |access-date=2016-03-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130426172142/http://www.im.ufrj.br/doc/nachbin.htm|archive-date=2013-04-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Nachbin was born in [[Recife]], and is best known for [[Nachbin's theorem]].  He died, aged 71, in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. He went to primary school in Recife with Brazilian literary giant [[Clarice Lispector]]. He is featured in one of her short stories, called “As Grandes Punições” (The Great Punishments) in her book “Aprendendo a Viver,” by the Rocco publishing house.

Nachbin was a Ph.D. student of [[Laurent Schwartz]]<ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy|id=23883}}</ref> at the [[University of Chicago]]. His Ph.D. students include [[Francisco Antônio Dória]] and [[Seán Dineen]].<ref name="MG"/> His monographs ''Topology and Order'' and ''The Haar Integral'', both published by Van Nostrand-Reinhold in 1965, are regarded as exceptional expositions of the subjects. Overall he authored ten books, most of which were published internationally, and edited a dozen tomes of the prestigious [https://www.sciencedirect.com/bookseries/north-holland-mathematics-studies ''North-Holland Mathematical Studies''] series between 1970 and the early 1980s. He is best known for a Tauberian-type theorem ([[Nachbin's theorem]]) on the growth rate of [[analytic function]]s, and for the so-called [[Realcompact space|Hewitt–Nachbin space]], a topological linear space that is [[bornological]] in the [[compact-open topology]].

He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) of 1962 in Stockholm ("Résultats récents et problèmes de nature algébrique en théorie de l'approximation"), being the first Brazilian speaker at the ICM.<ref>International Mathematical Union (IMU) . [http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php "ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897"] 
{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |date=2017-11-24 }}. ''mathunion.org''. Retrieved on 8 July 2017.</ref>

*''Introdução à Álgebra'' (McGraw-Hill, 1971, in Portuguese)
